headline: Highest risk is B data leakage via broad network egress; A is a non-runnable content repo with no shared channel, so other risks are limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a non-runnable content-writing repository with no io_surfaces or capabilities, while B only exposes REST API egress. There is no documented shared channel, parser bridge, or default ingestion path between them, so a prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced. If an external orchestrator manually copies A's text into B, that would be outside the documented pair.
conditions: IF an external operator manually copies A-generated text into B as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between them, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected; do not bridge outputs through shared files.
Require explicit human review before any A text is pasted into B.
Use a provenance tag on any transferred text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no runtime surfaces, so it cannot leak data itself. B has broad network egress and REST API access, which can transmit whatever context it receives, but the pair lacks a documented shared workspace or sensitive data source. The main risk is accidental transfer of operator-provided content into B, not autonomous leakage from A.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive files into a shared workspace that B can read, leakage risk increases.
IF B is given confidential prompts or transcripts, its network egress can transmit them.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in any shared folder.
Review B's outbound destinations before use.
Use redacted prompts for B.
Separate workspaces per agent.
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and DLP scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or concurrency capabilities documented, and B only documents broad network egress plus REST API calls. There is no overlapping mutable resource, filesystem, git, or OAuth scope to contend over, so a capability-conflict pathway is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF A is later given write access to the same mutable resource as B, conflict risk appears.
IF an orchestrator grants both agents the same API credentials, overlap may emerge.
mitigations: Keep credentials separate.
Avoid shared writable directories.
Run each agent in its own workspace.
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing repo and B is an observability/evaluation tool with REST API access, but neither profile shows default automation where B blindly acts on A's outputs. Without a documented handoff, the cascade is only plausible if an operator wires A's text directly into B's workflow. That makes the pathway possible but not default.
conditions: IF A's generated text is fed into B without verification, cascading error risk increases.
IF B is configured to execute actions based on A's outputs, the blast radius grows.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between A and B.
Require citations for any claims passed from A to B.
Limit B to read-only evaluation mode.
Log and review any automated handoff.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for A-to-B payloads.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. A is a non-runnable open-source repo and B is an open-source tool with no data classes touched, so there is no evidenced compliance breach pathway in the pair as provided.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data, compliance analysis must be revisited.
IF deployment introduces jurisdiction-specific storage or retention rules, mismatch risk may appear.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair.
Document any jurisdictional constraints before deployment.
Review retention settings if data handling is added.
requires-engineering: add policy checks for residency and retention.
